item.title: Version 3.12.0
item.description:
neoloopy 3.12.0 (build 66)

Companion apps can now send you straight to a model, the Android app is back, and creating a model no longer needs a name. Everything in the [3.11.0 notes](3.11.0.md) and the [3.10.0 notes](3.10.0.md) still applies.

Scope

  • macOS and Android. The macOS app (DMG and Sparkle update) with the embedded neoloopy CLI and MCP server, and the Android app as a direct .apk. The app changes reach iPhone and iPad with the next iOS submission. Windows and Linux builds stay at 3.5.0.
  • Android moves from 3.5.0 to 3.12.0 in one step, so everything released for the other platforms since 3.5.0 arrives with it. The new .apk is signed with the same key as 3.5.0 and installs over it.

Open a note from another app (macOS)

  • neoloopy://open links. A link of the form neoloopy://open?vault=<folder>&note=<path in the vault> opens that model in neoloopy: a Graph Model file, a model folder, or any note inside a model folder. Companion apps such as Bainso use it to land you on the model you are reviewing.
  • A link only navigates. It opens a model exactly as clicking it in the models list does. It never creates a vault and never opens anything outside the vault. A link to another vault always asks first, names the folder, and tells you the CLI and MCP server will use that vault too. A link that arrives while a model is open asks before closing it, and anything with unsaved work keeps its own save prompt. Malformed links show one short message and do nothing else.
  • Details are in "Open a note from another app" in docs/mcp.md.

In the app

  • Create works without a name. The New model dialog shows "Untitled model" in its name field, but pressing Create without typing a name used to close the dialog and create nothing. It now creates a model named "Untitled model", and a second one when that name is taken.
  • Escape closes the game scenario dialog again. After a Preview or Save that took more than a moment, Escape stopped closing the scenario dialog. It now works throughout.

CLI

  • neoloopy --version reports the app version (3.12.0), as do the usage banner, schema and the MCP server's serverInfo. It used to say 1.0.0.
